findings.summary: Previously: isInvalidKey matched any HTTP 403 containing PERMISSION_DENIED, which Google sets for nearly every 403 cause, so an unrelated 403 (billing off, API not enabled, IAM/referrer restriction) would permanently disable a valid key. FIXED: isInvalidKey now requires HTTP 400 + /API_KEY_INVALID|API key not valid/ (Google's actual invalid-key signal). A 403 now logs 'key kept' and throws AiServiceUnavailableError without touching the pool. New test gemini-call-runner.spec.ts:59-66 sends a realistic 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "Billing is disabled" body on a single-key pool and asserts the key still serves the next call.

Previously: a vector-size/count mismatch threw before this.record(), losing the usage_records row for countTokens calls already billed. FIXED: record() now runs immediately after the Gemini calls settle, before the dimension check; gemini.client.spec.ts asserts the real token count is recorded even when the size check subsequently fails.

Not changed, by design, and accepted: segment ingestion is rejected (409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION) once a meeting leaves recording/paused/ended/queued (Phase 04 decision), so a changed-scope run never actually finds segments past the last chunked range in production; the tail branch is defensive. Now covered at the unit level by chunker.spec.ts:93-99 ("chunks segments that arrived after the last range"), which proves the branch's own logic even though the integration path that would reach it is architecturally closed off. Acceptable given the cited state-machine rule; the earlier note that nothing tested the branch no longer holds.

Not changed, and accepted: a changed-scope reindex still resets every processing_jobs row to pending, but chunk reconciles by content_hash and embed only touches embedding IS NULL rows, so re-running unaffected chunks makes zero Gemini calls regardless of step status. The original concern (future non-idempotent Phase 13-15 steps re-running wastefully) is a forward design note for whoever builds those phases, not a defect in this phase's own idempotency, which holds.
